name: SonicWall
evidence_summary: SonicWall sources evidence SD-WAN support on TZ/NSA/SM platforms and integrated SD-WAN/security features in firewall appliances.
cost_model: Public hardware/security bundle pricing often available via resellers; managed options partner-dependent.
key_differentiators: SD-WAN delivered via existing TZ, NSa and SM firewall appliances; familiar deployment for organisations standardised on SonicWall.
Strong SMB and mid-market positioning with reseller channel and public hardware pricing.
Integrated firewall and SD-WAN avoids separate appliances for smaller branches.
best_fit_for: SMB and mid-market organisations already running SonicWall firewalls.
Distributed branch estates where firewall-led SD-WAN is operationally simpler than a separate SD-WAN platform.
Buyers prioritising public pricing visibility and reseller channel options.
watch_outs: SASE and SSE capabilities have partial public evidence; depth should be confirmed in RFP.
Less suited to large enterprise multinational deployments requiring private backbone or PoP architectures.
Public cloud gateway and multi-cloud transit fabric capabilities are less prominent than cloud-native SASE vendors.
verification_notes: Re-verified 2026-07-29 against named primary sources. Every graded fact carries a source, a tier and a verbatim quote confirmed present on the cited page by an independent check. Industry, region, organisation-size and pricing evidence was sourced on the same basis. Facts that could not be sourced are published as unknown with the reason. The value_tier field is a Netify assessment of relative cost position, not a supplier claim: most of this market publishes no price. Sources found and rejected are listed at tier 4.

ai_capability.note: Capture ATP cloud sandboxing uses ML-based detection.

resilience.note: HA appliance pairs; cloud security depth depends on partner SSE.

profile.platform_architecture: SonicWall delivers SD-WAN as a feature of its TZ and NSa firewall series, managed through Network Security Manager, with Capture Security Center providing cloud visibility. The architecture is firewall-first: branch appliances steering traffic across links with security inline, suited to distributed estates standardising on SonicWall hardware. Cloud Secure Edge (from the Banyan Security acquisition) adds cloud-delivered access.
profile.security_sase: Security capability centres on the firewall stack: deep packet inspection including TLS, Capture ATP cloud sandboxing with RTDMI memory inspection, and content filtering. Cloud Secure Edge provides ZTNA and SWG for remote users on a security service edge model. CASB and DLP depth is lighter than enterprise SASE leaders, positioning SonicWall for SMB and mid-market rather than global enterprise SASE consolidation.
profile.service_support_channel: SonicWall is overwhelmingly channel and MSP led, with strong UK distribution and an MSSP programme including multi-tenant management. Education and retail are notable verticals. Support tiers run to 24x7 with partner-delivered managed services common.
profile.commercials_verdict: Appliance plus security subscription bundles with aggressive street pricing; Cloud Secure Edge licenses per user. The Netify verdict: shortlist SonicWall for cost-conscious SMB and mid-market estates, education networks and MSP-delivered branch security where firewall-based SD-WAN is sufficient. Global enterprises needing deep CASB, DLP and a large PoP fabric should look to the enterprise SASE tier.

vendor_faqs.q: Is SonicWall SD-WAN good enough for multi-site businesses?
vendor_faqs.a: For tens of sites with straightforward topologies, yes: link steering, failover and zero-touch deployment are included with the firewalls. Large or complex global WANs will outgrow it; that is not SonicWall's target buyer.

SonicWall's cloud-delivered access service from the Banyan acquisition: ZTNA and web security for remote users, managed from the cloud and licensed per user, extending SonicWall estates beyond the appliance perimeter.

Multi-tenant management, an MSSP licensing programme, broad UK distribution and price points that fit SMB budgets. For MSP-delivered branch security with SD-WAN included, it remains one of the most economical stacks.

shortlist_summary: SonicWall deliver SD-WAN via existing TZ, NSa and SM firewall appliances, which is a real advantage for organisations already standardised on SonicWall and a less compelling proposition for those that aren't. Typically shortlisted by SMB and mid-market businesses with an existing SonicWall estate looking to add SD-WAN capability without the cost and complexity of introducing new hardware.
cost_note: Firewall-led SD-WAN with aggressive SMB and mid-market street pricing; low cost where a SonicWall estate exists.
uk_basis: No UK HQ (US). Strong UK SMB and mid-market channel and distribution.

f01_fully_managed_service.quote: Managed Firewall Service, MPSS, gives you expert configuration, proactive firmware management, and 24/7 monitoring for your Gen 7 or Gen 8 firewall
f01_fully_managed_service.note: SonicWall itself operates MPSS, covering configuration, firmware management, 24/7 monitoring, notifications, monthly health reporting and enhanced support. That is a genuine first-party managed service, but it is scoped to the firewall estate rather than the whole SASE service, and design, deployment and migration are explicitly delivered by Advanced Services Partners (source 10), not by SonicWall. Graded partial because the provider does not own the full design-to-report lifecycle end to end.

f03_co_managed_service.note: The SecureFirst Service Provider Plan explicitly advertises co-managed NOC and SOC support, and MPSS lets the customer or MSP raise tickets to request non-critical changes while SonicWall handles critical firmware updates. Confidence is medium because the quote is a programme bullet rather than a described service definition, and no split-responsibility matrix is published.

f04_multi_tenant_msp_white_label_support.quote: SonicWall Unified Management is a single pane of glass tool purpose-built for MSPs, making managing complex security environments among multiple tenants easy and streamlined.
f04_multi_tenant_msp_white_label_support.note: Multi-tenancy and delegated MSP management are clearly documented across Unified Management, the Service Provider Plan single multi-tenant dashboard, and CSE customer stories citing centralised multi-tenant management. However, no page reviewed names branded or white-label portals, custom branding, or tenant templates. Graded partial on the branding limb of the definition.

f05_professional_services_and_migration_.quote: From basic remote installation support to complex migration projects, SonicWall Advanced Services Partners can meet your implementation needs.
f05_professional_services_and_migration_.note: Structured assessment, network design, project management, technology migration, staging, implementation and training are all published and cover the discovery-to-training span in the definition. But SonicWall attributes delivery throughout to SonicWall Advanced Services Partners rather than to SonicWall staff, and directs buyers to Find a Service Partner. Graded partner_integrated for that reason. No rollback-plan language was found on any page reviewed.

f07_lifecycle_management.quote: The SonicSentry team will handle critical firmware updates for you
f07_lifecycle_management.note: MPSS covers firmware patching as part of the service, and the published product lifecycle policy sets out Last Order Day, Active Retirement Mode, Limited Retirement Mode and End of Support phases, with firmware support and hardware warranty available through LRM for products holding an active support contract. Renewals and hardware replacement are entitlement-based rather than proactively managed on the customer's behalf, so confidence is medium.

f17_cellular_and_5g_support.quote: By using low-cost internet access (broadband, 3G/4G/LTE, fiber), organizations can cost-effectively replace expensive WAN connection technologies such as MPLS with SD-WAN.
f17_cellular_and_5g_support.note: Cellular is named only as a low-cost WAN transport option on the Secure SD-WAN page. No page reviewed mentions 5G at all, and the entry-level TZ firewall page and the SD-Branch page contain no cellular, modem, WWAN or failover references. SIM management and signal monitoring were not found anywhere. Graded partial: 3G/4G/LTE transport is evidenced, 5G and SIM/signal management are not.

f19_public_cloud_gateways.quote: All traffic is intelligently routed to the nearest global cloud Point of Presence (PoP), providing low latency and high performance
f19_public_cloud_gateways.note: SonicWall operates its own cloud PoP estate under the Cloud Secure Edge / Global Edge banner, enforcing SWG, CASB, DNS-layer security and ZTNA as a cloud service. This is SonicWall's own infrastructure (CSE originated from its Banyan Security acquisition and is now a SonicWall product), not a third party's gateway resold, hence yes rather than partner_integrated.

f20_private_pops_dedicated_pops.quote: Global Edge for fully managed cloud delivery or Private Edge for environments requiring local performance or regulatory needs.
f20_private_pops_dedicated_pops.note: Private Edge is offered in the Secure Private Access Advanced tier as a customer-hosted alternative to the shared Global Edge, deployable on Linux, SonicWall firewalls, Windows Server, Kubernetes and OVB, and positioned explicitly for local performance or regulatory need. That matches the customer-hosted and sovereign limb of the definition.

f21_private_global_backbone.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. The SASE use-case page claims it 'Optimizes traffic routing with low-latency global connectivity' and the Secure Internet Access page describes routing to the nearest cloud PoP, but neither states that inter-region traffic rides a SonicWall-owned or SonicWall-controlled backbone. I read the CSE, Secure Private Access, Secure Internet Access, SASE and SD-WAN pages plus the CSE documentation index, which rendered as a navigation shell only. Absence of a claim is not evidence of absence, so this is recorded as unknown rather than no.

f26_sla_backed_service_fabric.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. The Legal index lists no Service Level Agreement document. The Support Services page shows a section heading 'SR Severity Levels & Response Times' but the underlying commitments did not render in the fetched content, and the Contact Support page publishes no response or availability targets. MPSS offers after-hours emergency support for critical issues, which is a support description rather than a contractual commitment. Graded unknown rather than no because contractual terms may sit behind support agreement documents that were not retrievable.

f27_integrated_next_generation_firewall.quote: Signature updates for intrusion prevention, anti-malware, botnet, and content filtering refresh automatically from the Capture Cloud Platform, activated as part of security services.
f27_integrated_next_generation_firewall.note: SonicWall authors its own NGFW (SonicOS on TZ, NSa, NSsp and NSv platforms) with intrusion prevention, anti-malware, botnet and content filtering delivered natively from its own Capture Cloud Platform, plus inspection of encrypted traffic ('Every packet, including encrypted traffic, is actively inspected at full speed.'). This is first-party technology, not a resold third-party engine, hence yes rather than partner_integrated. Note the delivery form is an appliance or virtual appliance under a common platform and management plane rather than a cloud-only firewall as a service.

f33_data_loss_prevention.quote: Enforce strong email data loss prevention (DLP) & compliance
f33_data_loss_prevention.note: The only explicit DLP capability found sits in SonicWall's Hosted / Cloud Email Security product, which analyses outbound email content and attachments for sensitive data. That is a separate email security product, not the SASE or SSE data path. The CSE page claims protection against 'data leaks' via SWG and CASB, and the Secure Internet Access page does not mention DLP at all. Graded partial: inspection of content for sensitive data is evidenced for email egress only, and no alerting or exception-workflow detail was found on any page reviewed.

f40_managed_service_assurance.quote: SonicSentry MDR for Network puts the power of our 24/7 expert SOC behind perimeter devices like firewalls, switches, and access points.
f40_managed_service_assurance.note: A SonicWall-operated 24/7 SOC with proactive threat hunting and a published four-minute average 2024 response time is well evidenced, and the Service Provider Plan advertises 24/7 co-managed NOC and SOC support. MPSS adds proactive offline and local-change notifications plus monthly health and productivity reports. However, no page reviewed uses the words root cause analysis, structured service reviews or change governance, and NOC appears only as a programme bullet. Graded partial against the full definition.

delivery_model.quote: Managed Firewall Service, MPSS, gives you expert configuration, proactive firmware management, and 24/7 monitoring
delivery_model.note: SonicWall is primarily a technology vendor authoring firewalls, SonicOS and the Cloud Secure Edge SSE stack, but it also operates first-party managed services delivered by its own SonicSentry team (MPSS managed firewall, SonicSentry MDR/MXDR). Design, deployment and migration work is largely delivered through Advanced Services Partners rather than by SonicWall itself, so the model is genuinely mixed.

underlay_ownership.quote: By using low-cost internet access (broadband, 3G/4G/LTE, fiber), organizations can cost-effectively replace expensive WAN connection technologies such as MPLS with SD-WAN.
underlay_ownership.note: SonicWall positions its SD-WAN over customer-procured internet access (broadband, DSL, Ethernet, 3G/4G/LTE, fibre) and sells no circuits. No page reviewed offers SonicWall-supplied access, carrier services or circuit procurement. Confidence is medium because this rests on the absence of any circuit offering across the pages read rather than on an explicit statement that SonicWall does not supply underlay.

sse_layer_ownership.quote: SonicWall Secure Internet Access (SIA), part of the Cloud Secure Edge (CSE), delivers cloud-native security for internet-bound traffic, protecting your users and data from malicious websites, phishing, ransomware, and risky SaaS applications everywhere work happens.
sse_layer_ownership.note: The SSE stack (Cloud Secure Edge, comprising Secure Private Access for ZTNA and Secure Internet Access for SWG, CASB and DNS-layer security) is SonicWall's own branded platform, sold standalone or added to its own Gen 7 firewalls via a built-in connector, and run on SonicWall's Global Edge. No third-party security vendor is named as the engine on any page reviewed. Recorded as native. Context: CSE derives from SonicWall's acquisition of Banyan Security, but it is now SonicWall-owned technology rather than a partner or resale arrangement.

regulatory_documentation.note: The SonicWall Trust Center names specific attestations and certifications in its Compliance section: SOC 2 Type 2, FIPS 140-2, FIPS 140-3 and Common Criteria. Found: SOC 2 Type 2. Not found on any page reviewed: ISO 27001, NHS DSPT, DORA, NIS2. The Legal index also carries a Sub-Processor List and Privacy Statement but no ISO certificate reference.

pop_count.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. The Secure Internet Access page confirms a global cloud PoP estate but publishes no number, the Secure Private Access page names Global Edge and Private Edge without a location count, and the Cloud Secure Edge documentation index rendered as a navigation shell with no edge network topic. Web search was unavailable during this task because the session search budget was exhausted, so only directly fetched vendor pages were assessed.

sla_availability_pct.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. No availability percentage of any kind appears on the Cloud Secure Edge, Secure Private Access, Secure Internet Access, Support Services, Contact Support or Legal pages, and the Legal index lists no Service Level Agreement document. There is not even a generic marketing mention of 'an SLA' to downgrade from; the figure is simply absent from the material read.

sectors.healthcare.quote: As threat actors and state-sponsored ransomware gangs continue to target and disrupt healthcare services, every Healthcare Delivery Organization (HDO) worldwide is vulnerable to attack, risking the compromise of patient data.
sectors.healthcare.note: Meets the bar on three counts: a dedicated healthcare industry page, HIPAA named as a compliance target, and named customer case studies. The industry page carries Women's Center for Radiology (with named IT Director Michael Brown) and a Medium-Enterprise Health Care Company study; the wider library adds Magrabi Hospitals and Centers, described as having more than 32 hospitals and centers in five countries with a named IT Director. The page states SonicWall solutions help meet HIPAA requirements, which is a vendor claim of assistance and not an accreditation.

sectors.financial_services.quote: Trusted by more than 6,000 financial services organizations worldwide, SonicWall delivers robust, manageable network information security in financial services, with solutions that extend protection of network resources down to the branch level.
sectors.financial_services.note: Dedicated financial services industry page, which alone meets the yes bar. The 6,000 figure is an unaudited vendor claim with no third-party corroboration found. The industry page itself names no customer, but the case study library contains Apple Federal Credit Union, Delta Insurance, a savings and loan company and a health insurance company, and the Cloud Secure Edge page carries insurer Lemonade with a named CISO, Jonathan Jaffe.

sectors.retail_ecommerce.quote: Build consumer confidence with security that exceeds PCI compliance mandates
sectors.retail_ecommerce.note: Dedicated Retail & Hospitality industry page plus named retail customer case studies. The Blue Tomato case study page is titled 'Blue Tomato: Europe-Wide Security - for Network, Stores and Offices' with the description 'Learn how SonicWall seamlessly protects retail networks of any sizes against cyberattacks.' The library also holds Bashas, Petland, Telebrands, Supermercado Mialich and several studies whose slugs are prefixed 'retail-'. Note this is physical and multi-site retail throughout; no ecommerce-specific evidence was found.

sectors.manufacturing.quote: Gokaldas Exports is recognized as one of India's largest apparel manufacturers and exporters.
sectors.manufacturing.note: Graded on a single clearly sector-labelled named customer. There is no manufacturing industry page in SonicWall's Solutions by Industry navigation, so manufacturing is not a marketed vertical. Several other library entries look like manufacturers (Cavagna Group, a Turkish sugar producer, poultry producer Bupilic, Monte Carlo Fashions, Harsha Automotive) but their pages carry no sector label and their narratives are in PDFs blocked by robots.txt, so they were rejected. Confidence is medium because the grade rests on one page's meta description.

sectors.energy_utilities.quote: Deployment of SonicWall Secure Mobile Access has helped the district
sectors.energy_utilities.note: Deliberately not graded yes. There is no energy or utilities industry page in the Solutions by Industry navigation. The only candidate found across the whole case study library is Crestline Sanitation District, a water and wastewater district, and its page carries no sector label; a sanitation district is arguably local government rather than a utility. Department of Energy, Republic of the Philippines is a government ministry, not an energy operator, and was not counted here. A reviewer could reasonably downgrade this to unknown; partial reflects that a utility-type named customer exists but nothing frames energy or utilities as a served sector.

sectors.government_public_sector.quote: U.S. Government-certified cybersecurity solutions for administrative, intelligence, and military organizations and agencies.
sectors.government_public_sector.note: Strongest sector evidence in the set. Three separate government industry pages (federal, state, local) plus externally awarded accreditations listed on the federal page: FIPS 140-2, FIPS 140-3, COMMON CRITERIA, DoDIN APL, COMMERCIAL SOLUTIONS FOR CLASSIFIED (CSfC), USGv6 and IPv6 Ready Logo, and NDAA Section 889 compliance. Named public sector customers include Washington County Sheriff's Office, Lawrence County Department of Public Safety, LARES, Webel Technology, Department of Energy, Republic of the Philippines, Gulf County Florida Board of County Commissioners and Borough of Kutztown. No US federal agency is named as a customer, only the certifications.

sectors.education.quote: Colleges and universities are not just educational institutions
sectors.education.note: Two dedicated industry pages, K-12 and higher education, plus a large body of named institutions. The higher education page carries University of Dundee ('University Secures Its Network Against 323,000 Attacks Per Day'), University of Hawaii (TASI) and Endicott College. The K-12 page carries Ceiba Public Schools and states that products are eligible for E-rate and CARES Act ESSER funding. Ajman University adds a Middle East institution with 7,000-plus users. Education is comfortably the deepest vertical in the case study library.

sectors.transport_logistics.note: Searched specifically and found nothing that qualifies. There is no transport or logistics industry page in the Solutions by Industry navigation, which lists only Distributed Enterprises, Retail & Hospitality, K-12 Education, Higher Education, Healthcare, Financial Services, Federal, State Government and Local Government. The whole case study library was enumerated via three XML sitemaps and the nearest candidates were rejected: Miray Cruises and 'Full Speed Ahead For Safer Cruise Ships' are cruise operators graded as leisure rather than transport, P Parking has no readable content, and Waycool Foods and various distributors carry no logistics label. No airline, rail, freight, shipping line, 3PL or fleet customer was found.

sectors.professional_services.quote: Learn how XimpleIT used SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge to replace legacy VPNs, stop breaches, and deliver Zero Trust security for small law firms.
sectors.professional_services.note: Graded on legal-sector evidence specifically. The XimpleIT study names the legal industry and small law firms as the vertical served, delivered through a managed service provider rather than direct. Corroborated by Fosters Solicitors, a named law firm, delivered with named partner HFI Consulting. There is no professional services industry page. Note that much of the delivery here is partner-led, so a case could be made for partner_integrated; yes was chosen because the customers themselves are named and the sector is explicitly stated. Accountancy services firm MyCPE ONE also appears in the library but was not fetched.

sectors.hospitality_leisure.quote: Build consumer confidence with security that exceeds PCI compliance mandates
sectors.hospitality_leisure.note: Covered by the same dedicated Retail & Hospitality industry page as retail, plus named hospitality customers. Celtic Manor Resort has its own case study page titled 'Celtic Manor Resort: A Super Infrastructure for Superpowers', and Great American Restaurants is the case study SonicWall links from its homepage navigation. The library also holds 'Resort Adds Security and Reliability to Enhance Guest Experience' and Oncu Doner, described as securing hundreds of franchises. Confidence is medium because the narrative PDFs for both flagship hospitality studies are blocked by robots.txt on the assets host, so only titles could be verified. The quote shown is the industry page headline, which covers hospitality jointly with retail.

regions.uk_ireland.quote: The Cloud Secure Edge (CSE) Global Edge Network is distributed across our edge infrastructure providers, enabling us to use one of their 50+ global regions to provide fast and reliable connections to your users around the world.
regions.uk_ireland.note: Service delivery evidenced by named points of presence, not by an office. The Cloud Secure Edge PoP documentation lists London under Europe for both Secure Private Access and Secure Internet Access, and additionally lists Ireland as a Secure Internet Access PoP. Supported by two registered entities: SonicWall (UK) Limited in Basingstoke and a SonicWall site in Cork. UK-delivered case studies exist in the library (Bradford Grammar School, Bolton College, Luton College) though their pages do not state the country.

regions.europe.quote: The Cloud Secure Edge (CSE) Global Edge Network is distributed across our edge infrastructure providers, enabling us to use one of their 50+ global regions to provide fast and reliable connections to your users around the world.
regions.europe.note: The PoP documentation lists Frankfurt and Stockholm for Secure Private Access, and Frankfurt, Paris and Stockholm for Secure Internet Access. Corroborated by registered entities SonicWall GmbH in Munich and an office in Barcelona, and by continental case studies including Blue Tomato (Europe-wide), Alexander Buerkle, Eijerkamp, Alsco Italia, Scholengroep Sint Rembert and Ansfelden Municipality.

regions.north_america.quote: The Cloud Secure Edge (CSE) Global Edge Network is distributed across our edge infrastructure providers, enabling us to use one of their 50+ global regions to provide fast and reliable connections to your users around the world.
regions.north_america.note: Densest coverage of any region. Secure Private Access PoPs listed at Ashburn Virginia, Council Bluffs Iowa, Los Angeles California, Moncks Corner South Carolina, Montreal and The Dalles Oregon; Secure Internet Access PoPs at North Virginia, Ohio, Northern California, Oregon and Montreal. Corporate headquarters at 1033 McCarthy Blvd, Milpitas, California. The overwhelming majority of named case studies are US organisations, and Montreal gives Canadian coverage.

regions.asia_pacific.quote: The Cloud Secure Edge (CSE) Global Edge Network is distributed across our edge infrastructure providers, enabling us to use one of their 50+ global regions to provide fast and reliable connections to your users around the world.
regions.asia_pacific.note: Secure Private Access PoPs listed at Mumbai, Tokyo, Singapore and Sydney; Secure Internet Access adds Osaka and Seoul. Offices in Bengaluru, Tokyo, Singapore, Seoul and Taipei. Named regional customers include Gokaldas Exports in India, Department of Energy Republic of the Philippines, Hutt City Council in New Zealand, and Sri Lankan, Japanese and South Korean studies in the library.

regions.middle_east_africa.quote: Ajman University boosts connectivity and security with SonicWall, improving network efficiency, internet speeds and cyber protection for 7,000+ users.
regions.middle_east_africa.note: Graded partial deliberately. The Cloud Secure Edge PoP list contains no Middle East or Africa location, so cloud-delivered SSE traffic from this region must hairpin to Europe or Asia. Delivery here is appliance and partner based rather than PoP based. Evidenced by named regional customers (Ajman University in the UAE, Magrabi Hospitals and Centers, Midmac Contracting, The Africa Institute, and several South African schools) and by the registered entity SonicWall MEA FZ-LLC in Dubai Internet City. Strong presence, but not equivalent service delivery to the four regions graded yes.

regions.latin_america.quote: The Cloud Secure Edge (CSE) Global Edge Network is distributed across our edge infrastructure providers, enabling us to use one of their 50+ global regions to provide fast and reliable connections to your users around the world.
regions.latin_america.note: Sao Paulo appears as a point of presence in both the Secure Private Access and Secure Internet Access lists, which is direct in-region service delivery. Corroborated by the Holambra Cooperativa Agroindustrial case study, described as one of Brazil's leading agribusiness groups with 170 member companies, delivered with named local partner Informo, and by Universidad Autonoma de la Ciudad de Mexico and Supermercado Mialich in the library. No LATAM office is listed on the contact directory, and Sao Paulo is the only Latin American PoP, so coverage is Brazil-anchored.

regions.china_mainland.note: No mainland China point of presence appears in the Cloud Secure Edge PoP documentation, which is the only service-delivery coverage document SonicWall publishes. The Asia Pacific PoPs are Mumbai, Osaka, Seoul, Tokyo, Singapore and Sydney, none in mainland China. The only mainland China artefact found anywhere on the site is a sales address in the contact directory at Fudan Science and Technology Park Building, Shanghai, which is a sales office and not evidence of service delivery. No ICP licence, no local carrier partnership and no China-specific arrangement is published. The generic 50+ global regions claim was treated as evidence of nothing here, as instructed.

organisation_fit.large_global_enterprise.quote: Scalable security that leverages the power of cloud intelligence and designed for large distributed enterprises, data centers and service providers
organisation_fit.large_global_enterprise.note: There is an explicit product tier for this size, the NSsp Series, sold under a 'Large Enterprises' heading on the firewall family page, plus a Distributed Enterprises solution page. However no named large global enterprise customer was found anywhere in the case study library, which was enumerated in full. The largest named customers are mid-sized: Magrabi with 32 hospitals in five countries, Ajman University with 7,000-plus users, Gokaldas Exports, and an unnamed 'Global Restaurant Chain'. Graded partial rather than yes because the evidence is product positioning and not a demonstrated customer of that scale.

organisation_fit.mid_market.quote: Enterprise-grade protection for your small to mid-size business or branch office
organisation_fit.mid_market.note: Explicit product tiering by size on the firewall family page, with the NSa Series sold under a 'Mid-Sized Enterprises' heading and the TZ Series covering small to mid-size business. Corroborated by named case studies of this size, including 'Medium-Enterprise Health Care Company', 'SABMD Medium Enterprise Retail Company', Ajman University and Magrabi. This is visibly SonicWall's centre of gravity.

organisation_fit.small_business.quote: Best-in-class Threat Protection for your small office, home office, IoT and Micro-SMBs
organisation_fit.small_business.note: A dedicated entry-level product exists for this segment (TZ80), and the TZ series page states 'The SonicWall TZ series of firewalls is designed specifically for the needs of SMBs and branch locations, delivering enterprise-class security without the enterprise-grade complexity.' Reinforced by a large MSP-delivered SMB motion: the Cloud Secure Edge page carries 'Stronghold Data Secures SMBs with Cloud Secure Edge' with a named CTO, and the library holds 'Griffin Technology Group Strengthens SMB Cybersecurity with SonicWall' and 'Small Business Engineering Company'.

published_pricing.quote: delivering threat block rates on par or better than competitors at a fraction of the cost
published_pricing.note: No price is published anywhere on sonicwall.com. There is no pricing page (the /products/cloud-secure-edge/pricing path returns 404), no price list, no starting price and no published subscription tiers; the how-to-buy path resolves to a sales contact form. This grade therefore rests entirely on the supplier's own positioning language, which is consistently cost-led: the entry-level page contains the verified string 'at a fraction of the cost' and also 'Make SonicWall TZ firewall the start of enterprise savings', the firewall family page states 'Instead of buying, integrating, and maintaining separate tools, SonicWall delivers essential bundled services that cut licensing, integration, and operational costs significantly', and the SD-WAN page leads on 'Lower costs by replacing expensive MPLS connections with cost-effective broadband options such as Ethernet, DSL and 3G/4G'. Combined with a product range that starts at micro-SMB and SOHO, 'value' is the honest reading, but confidence is low because no transactable price was found from the vendor, a marketplace or an analyst. If a stricter standard is applied, 'unknown' is defensible.
